beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW: composer, the week's ask lands answered. Required fellows intro line first, then the AI-voice disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Laksh, and this video is about whether a reinforcement learning agent can beat a simple rule that plans from yesterday's traffic. The voice you hear is an AI voice. The project is my own work, built with help from Claude Code.
beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer: the week's ask and its three results

show.event: greeting and the week's ask type into the composer
running indicator, then three result lines land

output: best agent only ties same time yesterday

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW: the hesitant writer types the hope (it beats the rule) and corrects it to the result (it only ties).
beats.narration_text: Training an agent with P P O does not beat a good rule for free. My best agent only ties same time yesterday, and the data shows what to test next.

show.event: the writer types 'and it beats a good rule'
'beats' turns terracotta, is deleted, and 'only ties' is typed in its place

props.text:
Train an agent with PPO
and it beats a good rule.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the overview is typed token by token, so mid-beat frames are mostly cream by design.

beats.role_note: the earlier result as the bar for PPO (evidence.json curves at the 70% target)
beats.narration_text: Previously, on five apps it had never seen, a rule that plans from the same time yesterday cut late requests from five and a half percent, with the Kubernetes rule, to just over one percent. That rule is the bar.
beats.new_visual_element: two bars: late requests under the Kubernetes rule and under same time yesterday

show.event: headline and an empty axis
the Kubernetes bar grows to 5.47%
the same time yesterday bar grows to 1.17%
a gold line marks it as the bar to beat

beats.role_note: what the PPO agent sees, does and is scored on (env.py _obs, action space, reward)
beats.narration_text: This week I trained P P O agents with Stable Baselines 3. Each minute, the agent sees recent traffic, yesterday's traffic and its servers, and adds or removes up to five servers. Its reward is minus the server cost, minus a penalty for each late request.
beats.new_visual_element: the agent loop: 25 numbers in, a change of -5 to +5 servers out, the reward line

show.event: headline; three groups of input squares
arrow into the PPO box, arrow out to -5 .. +5 servers
the reward line: reward = -(server cost + penalty x late requests)

beats.role_note: the two agent kinds (train.py) and the 30-run sweep (modal_train.py)
beats.narration_text: I tried two kinds. Plain P P O learns to scale from nothing. Residual P P O starts from the same time yesterday rule and learns only a correction. I trained thirty agents on Modal's cloud computers: two kinds, five penalty sizes, three seeds each.
beats.new_visual_element: two lanes (plain, residual), then a 2 x 5 x 3 grid of 30 runs filling in

show.event: plain lane: inputs -> PPO -> action
residual lane: rule action + PPO correction -> action
30 squares fill in: 2 kinds x 5 penalties x 3 seeds

beats.role_note: results/ppo/*.json against the baselines at 40-80% targets, held-out apps (evidence.json curves, ppo)
beats.narration_text: Each method becomes a curve: cost against late requests on the five unseen apps. Lower and further left is better. No agent beats same time yesterday. The best one, residual P P O at the highest penalty, only ties it.
beats.new_visual_element: cost against late requests: Kubernetes, same time yesterday, plain PPO, residual PPO

show.event: axes; the two rule curves draw on
plain and residual PPO curves draw on, seed ranges as bars
the best residual point is ringed next to the rule's curve

beats.role_note: the weekly shape in the 14 days (evidence.json weekly)
beats.narration_text: Then I looked at each day's traffic. Days six, seven, thirteen and fourteen are the quietest, and day eight is the busiest: a weekly shape. On that day, same time yesterday plans from a quiet day.
beats.new_visual_element: 14 bars: median daily traffic of the 19 apps; quiet days grey, day 8 gold

show.event: headline and 14 bars grow
days 6, 7, 13, 14 fade to grey
day 8 turns gold; an arrow from day 7 to day 8: 'yesterday'

beats.role_note: the plan in the README (week of 16 Nov)
beats.narration_text: Two weeks give each app only one such day, too few to test it. So next, I test on real traces several weeks long, add a same time last week rule, and test the rules first. Then P P O gets another try.
beats.new_visual_element: a 14-day strip with one marked day, then a multi-week strip and the next steps

show.event: a two-week strip with one marked day
a strip several weeks long, a marked day after each weekend
three next steps tick in

beats.role_note: recap card; the narration carries the takeaway
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A learned agent is not better by default. Test it at the same cost, on data it never saw, and check whether your traffic repeats each day or each week.

show.event: the artifact card lists five lines, one per idea

artifactLines: The bar: same time yesterday, 1.17% late.
Best agent ties the rule at equal cost.
Days 6-7 and 13-14 are quiet; day 8 is busiest.
Next: weeks-long traces, same time last week.

beats.role_note: YOUR TURN LAW: one prompt the viewer can paste
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Here are four weeks of my service's requests per minute. For each day, tell me which predicts it better: yesterday, or the same day last week.
